Breakout cables give 4x25G and 4x10G. The exact list is in the Hardware Compatibility Tool" data-extension-slot="one slot for the EX4400-EM-4S, EX4400-EM-4Y or EX4400-EM-1C module" data-console="USB-C and RJ-45 (CON), both on the front" data-oob="MGMT RJ-45 on the front, 10/100/1000, with link activity and status lamps" data-usb="USB-A on the front" data-cloud="Juniper Mist Wired Assurance, and the Junos CLI and J-Web" data-seismic="Tested for Zone 4 earthquake according to NEBS GR-63-CORE, Issue 5" data-eol="none-announced" data-airflow="back-to-front" data-power="ac">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

The exact list is in the Hardware Compatibility Tool" data-extension-slot="one slot for the EX4400-EM-4S, EX4400-EM-4Y or EX4400-EM-1C module" data-console="USB-C and RJ-45 (CON), both on the front" data-oob="MGMT RJ-45 on the front, 10/100/1000, with link activity and status lamps" data-usb="USB-A on the front" data-cloud="Juniper Mist Wired Assurance, and the Junos CLI and J-Web" data-seismic="Tested for Zone 4 earthquake according to NEBS GR-63-CORE, Issue 5" data-eol="none-announced" data-airflow="back-to-front" data-power="ac">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="399.0mm" height="43.7mm" viewBox="0 0 399.0 43.7" data-device="ex4400-24x" data-view="right" data-weight="6.7 kg with no power supply, fan module or extension module (EX4400-24X and -24X-AFI); 6.65 kg for the -DC builds" data-depth-with-modules="430.0 mm with power supply and fan modules; 440.7 mm with an extension module as well" data-mounting="two-post kit EX-RMK in the box; four-post kit EX-4PST-RMK and wall kit EX-WMK separate" data-throughput="540 Gbps unidirectional, 1080 Gbps bidirectional" data-heat-dissipation="422.84 BTU/hr idle and 470.58 at 100 percent traffic with a 550 W AC supply; 463.76 and 497.86 with a 550 W DC supply" data-operating-temp="0 C to 45 C (32 F to 113 F)" data-storage-temp="-40 C to 70 C (-40 F to 158 F) in the shipping container" data-humidity="5 to 90 percent noncondensing" data-altitude="no performance degradation up to 1828.8 m (6000 ft) at 40 C" data-acoustic-noise="42.71 dB(A) typical with one 550 W AC supply and front-to-back airflow (Table 115)" data-cpu="quad-core x86" data-memory="4 GB DDR4 with ECC" data-storage="20 GB eMMC" data-virtual-chassis="up to 10 switches; the front QSFP28 ports are Virtual Chassis ports only after request virtual-chassis mode hgoe" data-macsec="AES-256 on all SFP and SFP+ network ports, on the native QSFP28 ports and on the extension module ports" data-optics-sfp-plus="10 GbE SFP+ and 1 GbE SFP transceivers; the exact list is in the Hardware Compatibility Tool" data-optics-qsfp28="The two front ports take 100GbE QSFP28 or 40GbE QSFP+ transceivers (40G from Junos OS 22.1R1). Breakout cables give 4x25G and 4x10G. The exact list is in the Hardware Compatibility Tool" data-extension-slot="one slot for the EX4400-EM-4S, EX4400-EM-4Y or EX4400-EM-1C module" data-console="USB-C and RJ-45 (CON), both on the front" data-oob="MGMT RJ-45 on the front, 10/100/1000, with link activity and status lamps" data-usb="USB-A on the front" data-cloud="Juniper Mist Wired Assurance, and the Junos CLI and J-Web" data-seismic="Tested for Zone 4 earthquake according to NEBS GR-63-CORE, Issue 5" data-eol="none-announced" data-airflow="back-to-front" data-power="dc">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

The exact list is in the Hardware Compatibility Tool" data-extension-slot="one slot for the EX4400-EM-4S, EX4400-EM-4Y or EX4400-EM-1C module" data-console="USB-C and RJ-45 (CON), both on the front" data-oob="MGMT RJ-45 on the front, 10/100/1000, with link activity and status lamps" data-usb="USB-A on the front" data-cloud="Juniper Mist Wired Assurance, and the Junos CLI and J-Web" data-seismic="Tested for Zone 4 earthquake according to NEBS GR-63-CORE, Issue 5" data-eol="none-announced" data-airflow="back-to-front" data-power="dc">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */

       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }

    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }

       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`

       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {

      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }

      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }

    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="399.0mm" height="43.7mm" viewBox="0 0 399.0 43.7" data-device="ex4400-24x" data-view="right" data-weight="6.7 kg with no power supply, fan module or extension module (EX4400-24X and -24X-AFI); 6.65 kg for the -DC builds" data-depth-with-modules="430.0 mm with power supply and fan modules; 440.7 mm with an extension module as well" data-mounting="two-post kit EX-RMK in the box; four-post kit EX-4PST-RMK and wall kit EX-WMK separate" data-throughput="540 Gbps unidirectional, 1080 Gbps bidirectional" data-heat-dissipation="422.84 BTU/hr idle and 470.58 at 100 percent traffic with a 550 W AC supply; 463.76 and 497.86 with a 550 W DC supply" data-operating-temp="0 C to 45 C (32 F to 113 F)" data-storage-temp="-40 C to 70 C (-40 F to 158 F) in the shipping container" data-humidity="5 to 90 percent noncondensing" data-altitude="no performance degradation up to 1828.8 m (6000 ft) at 40 C" data-acoustic-noise="42.71 dB(A) typical with one 550 W AC supply and front-to-back airflow (Table 115)" data-cpu="quad-core x86" data-memory="4 GB DDR4 with ECC" data-storage="20 GB eMMC" data-virtual-chassis="up to 10 switches; the front QSFP28 ports are Virtual Chassis ports only after request virtual-chassis mode hgoe" data-macsec="AES-256 on all SFP and SFP+ network ports, on the native QSFP28 ports and on the extension module ports" data-optics-sfp-plus="10 GbE SFP+ and 1 GbE SFP transceivers; the exact list is in the Hardware Compatibility Tool" data-optics-qsfp28="The two front ports take 100GbE QSFP28 or 40GbE QSFP+ transceivers (40G from Junos OS 22.1R1). Breakout cables give 4x25G and 4x10G. The exact list is in the Hardware Compatibility Tool" data-extension-slot="one slot for the EX4400-EM-4S, EX4400-EM-4Y or EX4400-EM-1C module" data-console="USB-C and RJ-45 (CON), both on the front" data-oob="MGMT RJ-45 on the front, 10/100/1000, with link activity and status lamps" data-usb="USB-A on the front" data-cloud="Juniper Mist Wired Assurance, and the Junos CLI and J-Web" data-seismic="Tested for Zone 4 earthquake according to NEBS GR-63-CORE, Issue 5" data-eol="none-announced" data-airflow="front-to-back" data-power="dc">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }

Breakout cables give 4x25G and 4x10G. The exact list is in the Hardware Compatibility Tool" data-extension-slot="one slot for the EX4400-EM-4S, EX4400-EM-4Y or EX4400-EM-1C module" data-console="USB-C and RJ-45 (CON), both on the front" data-oob="MGMT RJ-45 on the front, 10/100/1000, with link activity and status lamps" data-usb="USB-A on the front" data-cloud="Juniper Mist Wired Assurance, and the Junos CLI and J-Web" data-seismic="Tested for Zone 4 earthquake according to NEBS GR-63-CORE, Issue 5" data-eol="none-announced" data-power="ac">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }

    g[data-ref^='juniper/ex4400-fan-afo@'] .state-green { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='juniper/jpsu-550-c-ac-afo@'] .state-blinking-green { --led-color: #39b54a; }
    g[data-ref^='juniper/jpsu-550-c-ac-afo@'] .state-blinking-green { animation: portrayal-blink 1s linear infinite; }
    g[data-ref^='juniper/jpsu-550-c-ac-afo@'] .state-green { --led-color: #39b54a; }
</style>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="441.7mm" height="399.0mm" viewBox="0 0 441.7 399.0" data-device="ex4400-24x" data-view="bottom" data-weight="6.7 kg with no power supply, fan module or extension module (EX4400-24X and -24X-AFI); 6.65 kg for the -DC builds" data-depth-with-modules="430.0 mm with power supply and fan modules; 440.7 mm with an extension module as well" data-mounting="two-post kit EX-RMK in the box; four-post kit EX-4PST-RMK and wall kit EX-WMK separate" data-throughput="540 Gbps unidirectional, 1080 Gbps bidirectional" data-heat-dissipation="422.84 BTU/hr idle and 470.58 at 100 percent traffic with a 550 W AC supply; 463.76 and 497.86 with a 550 W DC supply" data-operating-temp="0 C to 45 C (32 F to 113 F)" data-storage-temp="-40 C to 70 C (-40 F to 158 F) in the shipping container" data-humidity="5 to 90 percent noncondensing" data-altitude="no performance degradation up to 1828.8 m (6000 ft) at 40 C" data-acoustic-noise="42.71 dB(A) typical with one 550 W AC supply and front-to-back airflow (Table 115)" data-cpu="quad-core x86" data-memory="4 GB DDR4 with ECC" data-storage="20 GB eMMC" data-virtual-chassis="up to 10 switches; the front QSFP28 ports are Virtual Chassis ports only after request virtual-chassis mode hgoe" data-macsec="AES-256 on all SFP and SFP+ network ports, on the native QSFP28 ports and on the extension module ports" data-optics-sfp-plus="10 GbE SFP+ and 1 GbE SFP transceivers; the exact list is in the Hardware Compatibility Tool" data-optics-qsfp28="The two front ports take 100GbE QSFP28 or 40GbE QSFP+ transceivers (40G from Junos OS 22.1R1). Breakout cables give 4x25G and 4x10G. The exact list is in the Hardware Compatibility Tool" data-extension-slot="one slot for the EX4400-EM-4S, EX4400-EM-4Y or EX4400-EM-1C module" data-console="USB-C and RJ-45 (CON), both on the front" data-oob="MGMT RJ-45 on the front, 10/100/1000, with link activity and status lamps" data-usb="USB-A on the front" data-cloud="Juniper Mist Wired Assurance, and the Junos CLI and J-Web" data-seismic="Tested for Zone 4 earthquake according to NEBS GR-63-CORE, Issue 5" data-eol="none-announced" data-power="ac">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }

  <style>

    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }

       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>
